blocks.text: Halo Daniel! Selamat datang kembali ke dunia React + TypeScript. Dokumen ini adalah **peta jalan terstruktur** yang akan membawa Anda dari “lupa banyak” sampai ke level mahir, lengkap dengan teori, contoh kode, dan proyek praktik.
Filosofi Pembelajaran

items: **Pahami “kenapa” sebelum “bagaimana”** — jangan hanya menghafal sintaks, pahami masalah apa yang diselesaikan.
**Tulis ulang kode**, jangan hanya membaca. Otak belajar lewat tangan.
**Bangun hal nyata** — setelah setiap modul, buat sesuatu kecil.
**TypeScript itu teman, bukan musuh** — anggap TS sebagai pair programmer yang mengingatkan kesalahan sebelum runtime.

blocks.text: Cara Pakai Dokumen Ini

**Setiap modul punya bagian “Latihan”** — WAJIB dikerjakan sebelum lanjut.
**Setiap modul punya bagian “Common Pitfalls”** — ini kesalahan umum yang saya sering lihat, hindari.
Buka editor (VSCode) sambil membaca. Jalankan setiap snippet kode.

modules.title: Pengenalan React & Cara Kerjanya
modules.summary: Sebelum React, memperbarui UI berarti memanipulasi DOM secara manual (imperative) — rawan bug karena kita harus mengingat setiap perubahan state dan…

blocks.text: The Why: masalah apa yang diselesaikan React?

Sebelum React, memperbarui UI berarti memanipulasi DOM secara manual (*imperative*) — rawan bug karena kita harus mengingat *setiap* perubahan state dan menyinkronkannya ke layar. React membalik ini menjadi **deklaratif**: Anda mendeskripsikan "seperti apa UI untuk state ini", dan React yang mengurus pembaruan DOM. Akibatnya kode lebih mudah diprediksi dan di-debug.

items: **Component-based** — UI dipecah menjadi potongan kecil yang dapat dipakai ulang & diuji terpisah.
**Declarative** — Anda menulis hasil akhir; React menghitung perubahan minimal.
**Virtual DOM & reconciliation** — React membandingkan pohon UI baru vs lama di memori, lalu menerapkan **perubahan seminimal mungkin** ke DOM nyata (operasi yang mahal).
**Unidirectional data flow** — data mengalir dari atas (parent) ke bawah (child) lewat props, sehingga sumber kebenaran jelas dan bug mudah dilacak.

blocks.text: menyentuh DOM nyata itu lambat. Dengan menghitung *diff* di memori dulu lalu membatch pembaruan, React menghindari *reflow/repaint* berlebih. Anda tidak mengelola DOM — Anda mengelola **state**, dan UI adalah fungsi dari state: `UI = f(state)`.

modules.summary: The Why. React adalah JavaScript — bukan bahasa baru.

blocks.text: **The Why.** React adalah JavaScript — bukan bahasa baru. Mayoritas "kesulitan React" pemula sebenarnya kesulitan JavaScript. Kuasai ini lebih dulu karena dipakai di **hampir setiap** komponen.

React mendeteksi perubahan dengan membandingkan *referensi*. `arr.push(x)` mengubah array yang sama (referensi tetap) sehingga React **tidak** re-render. Selalu buat objek/array **baru**: `[...arr, x]`, `{...obj, k: v}`. Inilah alasan `spread` ada di mana-mana.

modules.summary: Vite adalah build tool modern yang super cepat.

blocks.text: Bagian 1: Setup Vite + React + TypeScript
Kenapa Vite?
Vite adalah build tool modern yang super cepat. Dev server-nya hampir instan, hot reload-nya cepat sekali. Cocok untuk belajar dan produksi kecil-menengah.
Instalasi

blocks.code:
npm create vite@latest my-react-app -- --template react-ts
cd my-react-app
npm install
npm run dev

blocks.text: Penjelasan:

items: `--template react-ts` artinya template React dengan TypeScript.
Setelah `npm run dev`, buka `http://localhost:5173`.

blocks.text: Struktur Folder Default

blocks.code:
my-react-app/
├── public/              # aset statis (favicon, dll)
├── src/
│   ├── assets/         # gambar, svg, dll
│   ├── App.tsx         # komponen utama
│   ├── App.css
│   ├── main.tsx        # entry point
│   ├── index.css       # style global
│   └── vite-env.d.ts   # deklarasi tipe untuk Vite
├── index.html          # HTML root
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json       # konfigurasi TypeScript
├── tsconfig.node.json
└── vite.config.ts      # konfigurasi Vite

blocks.text: File Penting untuk Dipahami

`index.html` — entry HTML. Perhatikan ada `
` dan ``. Semua React akan di-inject ke `#root`.
`src/main.tsx` — tempat React “dipasang” ke DOM:

blocks.code:
import React from 'react'
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom/client'
import App from './App.tsx'
import './index.css'

ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <React.StrictMode>
    <App />
  </React.StrictMode>,
)

blocks.text: Perhatikan tanda `!` setelah `getElementById('root')` — ini **non-null assertion** TypeScript: Anda memberitahu TS “saya yakin ini tidak null, percaya saja”. Kalau Anda tidak yakin, lebih aman pakai:
Bagian 2: TypeScript Fundamentals (khusus untuk React)
TypeScript adalah superset JavaScript yang menambahkan **type system**. Tujuannya menangkap bug saat menulis kode, bukan saat runtime.
Tipe Primitif

blocks.code:
let nama: string = "Daniel"
let umur: number = 25
let aktif: boolean = true
let hobi: string[] = ["baca", "coding"]       // array of string
let koordinat: [number, number] = [10, 20]    // tuple: array dengan panjang & tipe tetap
let apapun: any = "hindari ini"                // hindari 'any' sebisa mungkin
let belumTahu: unknown = fetchData()           // lebih aman dari any

blocks.text: **Aturan emas**: hindari `any`. Kalau benar-benar tidak tahu tipenya, pakai `unknown` — TS akan memaksa Anda cek tipe sebelum memakainya.
Object & Interface vs Type Alias
Untuk mendefinisikan “bentuk” object, ada dua cara:

**Kapan pakai yang mana?** - `interface` lebih cocok untuk bentuk object yang mungkin di-extend. - `type` lebih fleksibel — bisa untuk union, intersection, mapped types, dll. - Praktik umum saat ini: **pakai** `type` **sebagai default**, pakai `interface` hanya kalau butuh declaration merging atau extend class.
Union, Intersection, & Literal
Literal type (seperti `"loading"`) sangat powerful — gunakan untuk nilai terbatas (mirip enum).
Function Typing
Optional & Default Parameter
Generics (SANGAT PENTING)
Generic memungkinkan Anda menulis kode yang bekerja untuk banyak tipe, sambil tetap type-safe.
Generic akan muncul sangat sering di React (contohnya `useState<T>`). Pahami konsep ini baik-baik.
Utility Types yang Sering Dipakai

blocks.code:
type User = { id: number; name: string; email: string; age: number }

type UserNoAge = Omit<User, "age">              // tanpa age
type OnlyIdName = Pick<User, "id" | "name">     // hanya id & name
type PartialUser = Partial<User>                // semua field jadi opsional
type RequiredUser = Required<User>              // semua field wajib
type ReadonlyUser = Readonly<User>              // tidak bisa diubah

type UserKey = keyof User                        // "id" | "name" | "email" | "age"
type AgeType = User["age"]                       // number

blocks.text: Type Narrowing
TypeScript “mempersempit” tipe setelah pengecekan:
Pattern ini sangat berguna saat handling data dari API.
as (Type Assertion)

blocks.code:
const input = document.getElementById("myInput") as HTMLInputElement
console.log(input.value)  // TS tahu ini input, ada .value

blocks.title: Peringatan
blocks.text: `as` bilang ke TS “percaya aku”, jadi bisa salah kalau Anda salah assert. Gunakan hanya kalau perlu.
Bagian 3: Konfigurasi TypeScript untuk React
Buka `tsconfig.json` — ini “otak” TypeScript. Beberapa opsi penting:
`strict: true` mengaktifkan serangkaian pengecekan ketat. Awalnya menyebalkan, tapi ini yang membuat TypeScript benar-benar berguna. Jangan dimatikan.
Bagian 4: Path Alias (Opsional tapi Direkomendasikan)
Daripada menulis `import Button from "../../../components/Button"`, kita bisa pakai alias:

blocks.code: tsconfig.json:
vite.config.ts:

blocks.text: Sekarang bisa pakai: `import Button from "@/components/Button"`.
Latihan Modul 1

items: **Buat proyek baru** dengan Vite + React + TS. Jalankan dan pastikan tampil.
**Hapus semua isi** `App.tsx` dan tulis ulang komponen sederhana yang menampilkan nama Anda.
**Tulis fungsi TypeScript** dengan generic: `last<T>(arr: T[]): T | undefined` yang mengembalikan elemen terakhir array.
**Buat type** untuk merepresentasikan struktur `Todo`: `{ id: number, text: string, completed: boolean, priority?: "low" | "medium" | "high" }`.
**Konfigurasi path alias** `@/*` lalu buat satu komponen di `src/components/Hello.tsx` dan import di `App.tsx` pakai alias.

blocks.text: Common Pitfalls

items: **Matikan** `strict` **karena “error mulu”** — JANGAN. Fix error-nya, itu yang bikin Anda naik level.
**Pakai** `any` **karena buru-buru** — ini menghilangkan manfaat TypeScript. Pakai `unknown` kalau benar-benar butuh fleksibilitas.
**Lupa restart VSCode** setelah ubah `tsconfig.json` — kadang perlu “Restart TS Server” (Cmd+Shift+P → “TypeScript: Restart TS Server”).
**Mengira** `interface` **dan** `type` **persis sama** — untuk 90% kasus memang sama, tapi `type` bisa union/intersection, `interface` bisa declaration merging.

modules.title: React Fundamentals dengan TypeScript
modules.summary: React adalah library untuk membangun UI dengan pendekatan komponen.

blocks.text: Bagian 1: Apa itu React?

React adalah library untuk membangun UI dengan pendekatan **komponen**. Konsep intinya: 1. **UI = f(state)** — tampilan adalah fungsi dari data. 2. **Deklaratif** — Anda mendeskripsikan “seperti apa UI seharusnya”, bukan “bagaimana cara mengubahnya”. 3. **Komponen** — bagian UI yang reusable, punya state sendiri, dan composable.
Bagian 2: JSX
JSX adalah sintaks “HTML di dalam JavaScript”. Sebenarnya JSX dikompilasi menjadi pemanggilan fungsi `React.createElement()`.
Aturan JSX yang Sering Dilupakan

items: Hanya boleh **satu root element**. Pakai `<></>` (Fragment) kalau butuh dua.
Pakai `className`, bukan `class`.
Pakai `htmlFor`, bukan `for`.

Self-closing: ``, `
`, `` — wajib ada `/`.
Style inline pakai object: `<div style={{ color: "red", fontSize: 14 }}>`.
Komentar di JSX: `{/* komentar */}`.

blocks.text: Embed Ekspresi JavaScript
Pakai `{}` untuk menyisipkan JS:

blocks.title: Penting
blocks.text: di antara `{}` hanya boleh **ekspresi**, bukan statement (tidak boleh `if`, `for`, `let`, dll).
Bagian 3: Komponen Fungsional
Komponen modern di React adalah **function component**. Lupakan class component (kecuali Anda maintain kode lama).
**Nama komponen WAJIB diawali huruf kapital.** Kalau huruf kecil, React menganggapnya sebagai HTML tag biasa.
Cara Pakai Komponen
Bagian 4: Props dengan TypeScript
Props = parameter ke komponen. Cara mendefinisikan props dengan TS:
Children Prop
Kalau komponen punya children (konten di dalam tag), pakai tipe `React.ReactNode`:
`ReactNode` adalah tipe paling fleksibel untuk children: bisa string, number, JSX, array, null, dll.
Props dengan Default Value
Spread Props
Kadang Anda ingin meneruskan semua attribute HTML ke elemen. Pakai `ComponentProps`:
Pattern `ComponentProps<"tag">` SANGAT berguna untuk membuat komponen wrapper.
Bagian 5: useState — State Dasar
State adalah data yang berubah seiring waktu. Tiap perubahan state memicu re-render.
TypeScript & useState
TS akan **infer** tipe dari nilai awal:

blocks.code:
const [count, setCount] = useState(0)        // number
const [name, setName] = useState("")          // string
const [active, setActive] = useState(false)   // boolean

blocks.text: Kalau nilai awal `null` atau bisa lebih dari satu tipe, **eksplisit**:
Functional Update
Kalau state baru bergantung pada state lama, pakai **functional update**:
Kenapa? Karena `setState` itu async. Kalau Anda panggil 3x berturut-turut:

blocks.code:
setCount(count + 1)
setCount(count + 1)
setCount(count + 1)
// hasil: count hanya naik 1, bukan 3!

setCount(prev => prev + 1)
setCount(prev => prev + 1)
setCount(prev => prev + 1)
// hasil: count naik 3 ✓

blocks.text: State Object & Array (IMMUTABILITY!)
**ATURAN PALING PENTING DI REACT**: jangan pernah mutasi state. Selalu buat object/array BARU.
Hafalkan pola ini sampai jadi otot:

items: **Tambah ke array**: `[...arr, baru]`
**Hapus dari array**: `arr.filter(x => kondisi)`
**Update satu item**: `arr.map(x => kondisi ? newX : x)`
**Update object**: `{...obj, field: newValue}`

Tipe Event yang Sering Dipakai

blocks.text: Anda bisa juga inline tanpa type annotation, TS akan infer otomatis:

blocks.code: <input onChange={(e) => setText(e.target.value)} />

Bagian 8: Rendering List
Aturan Key

items: **Key WAJIB ada** saat render list.
**Key harus unik** di antara siblings.
**JANGAN PAKAI INDEX** sebagai key kecuali list-nya statis (tidak diurutkan/difilter/ditambah/dihapus).

blocks.text: Bagian 9: Controlled vs Uncontrolled Input
**Controlled** (direkomendasikan): nilai input dikelola React state.
**Uncontrolled**: nilai input dikelola DOM, akses pakai ref.
90% kasus: pakai controlled. Uncontrolled berguna untuk integrasi library non-React, file input, performance pada form besar.
Bagian 10: Composing Components
Komponen bisa berisi komponen lain. Inilah cara membangun UI kompleks:
Latihan Modul 2

items: **Counter**: Buat counter dengan tombol +1, -1, dan reset. Tambahkan validasi: count tidak boleh < 0.
**TodoList**: Buat aplikasi todo dengan input untuk tambah todo, list todo, tombol toggle done, tombol hapus.
**Filter**: Tambahkan filter di TodoList: “all”, “active”, “completed”.
**Card Component**: Buat komponen `<Card title="..." footer={...}>{children}</Card>` dengan props yang di-type dengan baik.
**TypedInput**: Buat komponen `<Input>` yang spread semua props HTML ke `<input>` + label di atasnya.

blocks.text: Common Pitfalls

items: **Mutasi state langsung** — selalu pakai `setState` dengan object/array baru.
**Pakai index sebagai key di list yang dinamis** — bisa menyebabkan bug aneh saat reorder/delete.
**Memanggil setState di dalam render body** — akan infinite loop. Setstate hanya boleh di event handler atau effect.
**Lupa** `e.preventDefault()` **di onSubmit** — halaman akan reload.
**Conditional rendering dengan** `&&` **dan angka** — `0 && <Comp />` render “0”.

modules.title: Hooks Lengkap
modules.summary: Hooks adalah fungsi spesial yang “menyambungkan” komponen ke fitur React (state, lifecycle, context, dll).

blocks.text: Hooks adalah fungsi spesial yang “menyambungkan” komponen ke fitur React (state, lifecycle, context, dll).
Aturan Hooks (PENTING)

items: **Hanya panggil di top level komponen** — jangan di dalam if/loop/nested function.
**Hanya panggil dari React function** — dari komponen, atau custom hook lain.
**Nama custom hook harus diawali** `use` — contoh: `useAuth`, `useFetch`.

blocks.text: ESLint plugin `react-hooks` akan menangkap pelanggaran aturan ini. Pasang!
useState (Review Cepat)
Sudah dibahas di modul 2. Ringkasan:

blocks.code: const [state, setState] = useState<T>(initialValue)

blocks.text: Lazy Initial State
Kalau initial value butuh komputasi mahal, pakai fungsi:
useEffect — Side Effects
`useEffect` untuk efek samping: fetch data, subscribe event, mengubah DOM, timer, dll.
Dependency Array
Aturan:

items: **Tidak ada** `[]` → effect jalan setiap render (jarang dipakai, hampir selalu salah).
`[]` **kosong** → jalan sekali saat mount, cleanup saat unmount.
`[deps]` → jalan saat mount + setiap kali salah satu deps berubah.

blocks.text: Cleanup Function
Return function dari useEffect untuk membersihkan effect:
Pattern: Fetch Data dengan AbortController
Ini mencegah race condition kalau `userId` berubah cepat sebelum fetch selesai.
Common Mistakes useEffect

items: **Lupa cleanup** → memory leak (event listener menumpuk, timer tidak berhenti).
**Dependency array tidak lengkap** → bug stale value. Pasang ESLint `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`!
**useEffect untuk computed value** → SALAH. Pakai variable biasa atau `useMemo`.

blocks.text: useRef — Mutable Value & DOM Access
`useRef` untuk dua kasus: 1. Akses DOM element. 2. Menyimpan nilai mutable yang TIDAK memicu re-render.
Akses DOM
Mutable Value (tidak trigger render)
Perbedaan useRef vs useState
useMemo — Memoize Hasil Komputasi

**Kapan pakai** `useMemo`**?** - Komputasi mahal (sorting/filtering data besar). - Saat hasilnya jadi dependency hook lain (atau prop ke komponen yang di-memo). - **JANGAN** memo semua hal — overhead memo bisa lebih mahal dari komputasinya.
useCallback — Memoize Function
`useCallback(fn, deps)` setara dengan `useMemo(() => fn, deps)`. Berguna saat function:

items: Di-pass ke komponen yang di-`React.memo()`.
Jadi dependency `useEffect` lain.

blocks.text: **Sama seperti** `useMemo`: jangan dipakai sembarangan, hanya kalau ada manfaat performance jelas.
useReducer — State Management Lokal yang Kompleks
Saat state banyak field & banyak transition, `useReducer` lebih bersih dari banyak `useState`.
**Pattern penting**: Action sebagai discriminated union (`type: "..."` field). TS akan auto-narrow di setiap case.
useContext — Berbagi State Antar Komponen
Context untuk berbagi data tanpa prop drilling.
**Pattern bagus**: jangan langsung export `Context`, tapi export Provider + custom hook (`useTheme`). Ini lebih aman & ergonomis.

blocks.title: HATI-HATI
blocks.text: Context yang nilainya sering berubah akan men-trigger re-render semua consumer. Jangan masukkan SEMUA app state ke satu context — pisah per concern.
useLayoutEffect — Sebelum Browser Paint
Mirip `useEffect`, tapi dijalankan **sinkron setelah DOM update, sebelum browser paint**. Pakai untuk pengukuran DOM yang harus diaplikasikan sebelum user lihat layar.
**Aturan praktis**: pakai `useEffect` dulu. Hanya ganti ke `useLayoutEffect` kalau ada flicker visual.
useId — ID Unik untuk Aksesibilitas
Saat butuh ID unik untuk hubung label-input atau ARIA:
Aman untuk SSR (server-side rendering).
Custom Hooks (Yang Membuat Kode Bersih)
Custom hook = fungsi yang menggunakan hooks lain. Tujuannya: **reuse logic stateful** antar komponen.
Contoh 1: useToggle
`as const` di akhir penting agar TS tahu return-nya tuple, bukan array biasa.
Contoh 2: useDebounce
Contoh 3: useFetch
Pattern **discriminated union state** seperti di atas adalah cara TS-friendly menangani async state. Catatan: untuk produksi, pakai TanStack Query (dibahas di modul 4) — lebih lengkap.
Contoh 4: useLocalStorage
Aturan Bagus untuk Custom Hooks

items: **Nama harus mulai dengan** `use` (wajib agar React tahu).
**Return tuple** (seperti `useState`) untuk hook dengan beberapa value.
**Return object** kalau lebih dari 3 value.
**Generic** kalau menerima/mengembalikan tipe data dinamis.
**Single responsibility** — satu hook satu concern.

blocks.text: Latihan Modul 3

items: `useCounter`: custom hook dengan return `{ count, increment, decrement, reset, setCount }`.
`useWindowSize`: hook yang mengembalikan `{ width, height }` window dan update saat resize. Jangan lupa cleanup!
`useOnlineStatus`: hook yang mengembalikan `boolean` apakah user online (pakai event `online`/`offline`).
`useClickOutside`: hook yang menerima ref dan callback, panggil callback kalau user klik di luar element.
**TodoApp dengan useReducer**: refactor TodoApp dari modul 2 untuk pakai `useReducer` dengan action: ADD, TOGGLE, DELETE, EDIT, CLEAR_COMPLETED.

blocks.text: Common Pitfalls

items: **Memanggil hook bersyarat**: `if (x) { useState(...) }` — DILARANG.
**Lupa dependency** di useEffect/useMemo/useCallback — bug stale value.
**Object/array sebagai dependency** — referensi berubah tiap render. Pakai useMemo untuk stabilkan, atau primitive value sebagai deps.
**useState untuk derived state** — derive saja saat render: `const fullName =`${first} ${last}\`\`.
**Custom hook tanpa cleanup** — kalau ada subscription/timer, harus return cleanup.

modules.summary: Hook yang jarang dibahas di kursus dasar: useInsertionEffect, useTransition, useDeferredValue, useDebugValue, useSyncExternalStore, dan hook baru React 19.

blocks.text: useLayoutEffect & useInsertionEffect
useLayoutEffect

Menunda pembaruan sebuah nilai non-urgent. Mirip useTransition, tetapi untuk nilai, bukan untuk pembungkus fungsi update.

Saat kamu hanya punya 'nilai' (mis. prop dari induk) dan ingin menunda render berat yang bergantung padanya.
Pasangan alami untuk komponen daftar berat yang dibungkus React.memo.

React 19 menambah hooks untuk menangani aksi asinkron, form, dan optimistic UI dengan boilerplate jauh lebih sedikit.

modules.summary: Saat aplikasi tumbuh, mengelola state hanya dengan useState jadi sulit.

blocks.text: Saat aplikasi tumbuh, mengelola state hanya dengan `useState` jadi sulit. Modul ini bahas 4 pendekatan: Context API, Zustand, Redux Toolkit, dan TanStack Query.
Kapan Butuh State Management Eksternal?

Tanyakan dulu: 1. Apakah state ini dipakai banyak komponen yang tidak berkerabat? 2. Apakah ada prop drilling 3+ level? 3. Apakah state ini perlu persisten / sinkron antar tab? 4. Apakah ini server state (data dari API) atau client state (UI state)?
Jawaban menentukan tools:

items: **Server state** (data dari API) → **TanStack Query** atau SWR.
**Client state simple** (theme, auth, modal) → **Context API**.
**Client state kompleks/tersebar** → **Zustand** (sederhana) atau **Redux Toolkit** (enterprise, devtools, time-travel).

blocks.text: **Pisahkan server state dari client state**. Banyak orang dulu pakai Redux untuk menyimpan data API — itu menyebabkan banyak boilerplate (loading, error, refetch, cache). TanStack Query menyelesaikan masalah ini.

blocks.text: **Pattern paling umum di proyek React modern:** - Server state → TanStack Query. - Client state simple → Context / Zustand. - Form state → React Hook Form.
Latihan Modul 4

items: **Auth dengan Context**: implementasikan `AuthProvider` lengkap dengan login/logout (boleh fake API).
**Cart dengan Zustand**: implementasikan store cart seperti contoh, plus persist ke localStorage.

**Optimasi Context**: buat 2 component yang konsumsi context yang sama. Pisah jadi state context + dispatch context. Pakai React DevTools Profiler untuk verifikasi tidak ada re-render tidak perlu.

blocks.text: Common Pitfalls

items: **Pakai Redux untuk semua state** — overkill, banyak boilerplate. Mulai kecil.
**Memasukkan server state ke Zustand/Redux** — bagus tidak salah, tapi reinventing TanStack Query.
**Subscribe seluruh store di Zustand** — re-render banyak. Selalu pakai selector.
**Lupa** `invalidateQueries` **setelah mutation** — UI tidak update.
`queryKey` **tidak unik / typo** — cache miss / share cache yang salah.

modules.title: Re-render & Memoization
modules.summary: Kapan komponen re-render, cara kerja React.memo, useMemo, useCallback, dan pola mencegah render yang tidak perlu.

blocks.text: Memahami Re-render (Fondasi)

Optimasi dimulai dari paham KENAPA komponen re-render. Komponen React render ulang saat: state-nya berubah, props-nya berubah, atau induknya render ulang. Render ulang itu normal dan biasanya murah — masalah baru muncul bila render berat atau terjadi terlalu sering.
Jangan optimasi sebelum ada masalah terukur. Tulis kode bersih dulu, ukur dengan Profiler, baru optimasi titik yang lambat.
blocks.title: Kegunaan & kapan dipakai

blocks.text: React.memo
Membungkus komponen agar hanya render ulang bila props-nya benar-benar berubah (perbandingan dangkal).

Komponen yang sering dirender induknya padahal props-nya jarang berubah, terutama di dalam list panjang.
Agar efektif, props fungsi/objek harus stabil (lihat useCallback/useMemo) — atau biarkan React Compiler yang urus (Bab 31).
blocks.title: Kegunaan & kapan dipakai

blocks.text: useMemo & useCallback (Kapan Masih Perlu)

Keduanya sudah dibahas di Bagian A. Inti optimasinya: useMemo mencegah komputasi ulang yang berat; useCallback menjaga referensi fungsi stabil agar React.memo bekerja dan dependency efek tidak berubah percuma.

blocks.code: const onClick = useCallback((id) => pilih(id), [pilih]); // cache fungsi
blocks.title: const data = useMemo(() => olahBerat(raw), [raw]);   // cache nilai

blocks.text: Memoization juga punya biaya (memori + perbandingan). Memasangnya di mana-mana bisa MEMPERLAMBAT. Pakai hanya bila terbukti membantu — atau serahkan ke React Compiler.

blocks.text: Ringkasan Visual: Lazy Loading in React
👉 A must-know technique to improve performance by loading components and resources only when needed.
What is Lazy Loading?
Lazy Loading is a design pattern where components or resources are loaded only when they are required, rather than at the initial load of the application.
React provides a built-in way to implement lazy loading using the React.lazy() function.

blocks.code: const LazyComponent = React.lazy(() => import('./LazyComponent'));

blocks.text: Lazy Loading a Component
Here’s how you can lazy load a React component with a fallback for while it’s loading:

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: 💡 Tip: Always wrap lazy-loaded components with Suspense to show a fallback during loading.
Lazy Loading with Routes
For route-based lazy loading, combine React.lazy() with a router like react-router-dom.
Preloading
While lazy loading improves performance, preloading can be used to further enhance the user experience.
Preload components when they are likely to be needed soon:
This technique ensures the component is ready by the time the user interacts with it!
Conclusion
Use lazy loading when:

items: You have components or routes that are not immediately visible to the user.
Your app has large third-party libraries that can be loaded only when needed.

blocks.text: Avoid lazy loading for critical components that are needed immediately on page load.

blocks.text: React Compiler (Informasi Lanjutan 2026)

Ini perkembangan terbesar untuk performa React. React Compiler (sebelumnya 'React Forget') adalah alat build-time yang otomatis menambahkan memoization yang setara dengan useMemo, useCallback, dan React.memo — tanpa kamu menulisnya sama sekali. Versi 1.0 rilis akhir 2025 dan kini didukung stabil di Next.js dan Vite, bahkan aktif default di sebagian template.
Cara Kerja Singkat

Compiler menganalisis komponen secara statis, membangun grafik dependency untuk tiap ekspresi, lalu menyisipkan cache pada level 'reactive scope' — sering lebih granular daripada memoization manual. Kamu menulis kode lugas; compiler mengurus optimasinya.

Tab 'Highlight updates' di DevTools: melihat komponen yang re-render secara visual.

Badge 'Memo ✨' di DevTools menandakan komponen yang dioptimalkan React Compiler.

blocks.text:
Kamu kini punya gambaran lengkap dan terapan: semua hooks beserta kegunaannya, seluruh tingkatan state management dari useState sampai React Query, dan teknik optimasi dari React.memo sampai React Compiler.
Kunci menjadi mahir: mulai sederhana, naik level hanya saat perlu, ukur sebelum mengoptimasi, dan biarkan alat modern (React Compiler, React Query) menanggung pekerjaan berat. Praktikkan di proyek nyata — itu cara belajar tercepat. Selamat berkarya!

blocks.text: Server Components vs Client Components
**Default di App Router: SEMUA komponen adalah Server Component.**
Server Component

items: Render di server.
Bisa async dan langsung await fetch.
Tidak bisa pakai hooks (useState, useEffect, dll).
Tidak bisa pakai event handler (onClick, dll).
Tidak dikirim ke browser sebagai JS — bundle lebih kecil.

blocks.text: Client Component
Tandai dengan `"use client"` di baris pertama.
Aturan Penting

items: **Mulai dari Server Component**, ganti ke Client hanya saat butuh interaktivitas.
**Server Component bisa import & render Client Component**.
**Client Component TIDAK bisa import Server Component** (kecuali di-pass sebagai children).
**Dorong Client Components ke “leaf”** — semakin kecil semakin baik untuk bundle size.

blocks.text: Pattern: Pass Server Component sebagai Children
Routing
Static Route
File `app/about/page.tsx` → URL `/about`.
Dynamic Route
File `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` → URL `/blog/anything`.
Sejak Next 15, `params` & `searchParams` jadi Promise. Wajib `await`.
Catch-all Route
`app/docs/[...slug]/page.tsx` → match `/docs/a`, `/docs/a/b`, dll.
Route Group (tidak mempengaruhi URL)
`app/(marketing)/about/page.tsx` → URL tetap `/about`. Berguna untuk grouping organisasi.
Parallel & Intercepting Routes
Advanced — lihat dokumentasi Next.js setelah dasar mantap.
Layout & Nested Layout
Layout di-share antar route. Saat navigasi, layout TIDAK remount — hanya children yang berubah.
Ini akan membungkus semua page di `/dashboard/*`.
Loading & Error UI
loading.tsx
Otomatis dibungkus `<Suspense>` saat page Anda async.
error.tsx
not-found.tsx
Data Fetching
Server-side (preferred)
Langsung di Server Component:
Opsi cache:

items: `cache: "force-cache"` (default) — static, cache selamanya sampai invalidate.
`cache: "no-store"` — selalu fetch fresh (dynamic).
`next: { revalidate: N }` — ISR, fresh tiap N detik.
`next: { tags: ["posts"] }` — tag untuk on-demand revalidation.

Server Action = function yang jalan di server, dipanggil dari Client/Server Component.
Tidak perlu API endpoint, tidak perlu fetch dari client. Powerful untuk form CRUD.

blocks.text: Common Pitfalls

items: `"use client"` **di top level layout** — semua jadi client. Hanya tandai komponen leaf yang butuh interaktivitas.
**Lupa** `await params` di Next 15 — error runtime.
**Pakai** `useState` **di Server Component** — error build. Tambah `"use client"`.
**Fetch tanpa caching strategy** — bisa lambat atau over-cache.
`process.env` **tanpa prefix di client** — `undefined` di browser.

Filosofi Testing untuk Frontend

**Testing Trophy** (Kent C. Dodds), dari paling banyak ke paling sedikit: 1. **Static** — TypeScript + ESLint sudah Anda pakai → ✓ 2. **Unit** — fungsi murni, custom hooks. 3. **Integration** — beberapa komponen kerja sama (paling penting!). 4. **E2E** — user flow full di browser (Playwright/Cypress).
Tulis test seperti user. Test apa yang user lakukan, bukan implementasi internal.

blocks.text: Report di `coverage/index.html`. Target praktis: **70-80% coverage**, jangan obsesi 100%.
Best Practices

items: **Test perilaku, bukan implementasi**. Hindari assert state internal.
**Tulis test yang gagal kalau user terdampak**. Kalau Anda rename variable internal, test tidak boleh pecah.
**Hindari snapshot testing** untuk komponen besar — sering jadi noise.
**Setup ulang state di tiap test** — jangan share state antar test (`afterEach(cleanup)` membantu).
**Mock minimal** — mock dependency external (API, time, random), jangan mock terlalu dalam.
**Test edge case** — list kosong, error, value extrim, network slow.

blocks.code: Test naming: it("[subject] [action] [expected outcome]") — eg it("submit form with valid data calls onLogin").

items: **Pakai** `describe` **untuk grouping** — lebih mudah baca report.

blocks.text: E2E lambat tapi memberi confidence tinggi. Pakai untuk **happy path** kritikal (login, checkout), bukan semua kemungkinan.

**Test TodoList**: integration test — add todo, toggle, delete, filter.
**Test Custom Hook** `useDebounce`: pakai `vi.useFakeTimers()` untuk control timer.
**Test Form Login**: termasuk error state ketika email kosong.
**Test API Component dengan MSW**: setup MSW, test komponen yang fetch user.

blocks.text: Common Pitfalls

items: `getByTestId` **di mana-mana** — pakai role/label, lebih maintainable.
**Tidak** `await` **userEvent** — assert dijalankan sebelum effect selesai.
**Mock terlalu dalam** — test kehilangan nilai. Mock hanya boundary (API, browser API).
**Test yang flaky** — biasanya karena timer/animasi tidak di-control. Pakai fake timers atau `findBy`.
`fireEvent` **instead of** `userEvent` — `fireEvent` tidak realistis (tidak trigger sequence event sebenarnya).

blocks.title: The Why feature-based

blocks.text: Composition Pattern
alih-alih satu komponen dengan 20 props boolean, susun dari bagian-bagian kecil lewat `children`/slot. Ini pola inti React untuk komponen yang fleksibel & dapat dipakai ulang.
blocks.title: Komposisi > konfigurasi

blocks.text: Error Boundary
**The Why.** Error saat render satu komponen bisa **menjatuhkan seluruh aplikasi** (layar putih). Error Boundary menangkapnya dan menampilkan UI cadangan, mengisolasi kerusakan.

blocks.code:
import { ErrorBoundary } from 'react-error-boundary'; Terjadi kesalahan.

}>

blocks.text: Pasang Error Boundary di sekitar area berisiko (widget pihak ketiga, route) — bukan hanya satu di root — agar kegagalan satu bagian tidak menghapus seluruh layar. (Error Boundary menangkap error *render*, bukan error di event handler/async — itu ditangani try/catch biasa.)

blocks.code:
// prisma/schema.prisma
generator client { provider = "prisma-client-js" }
datasource db { provider = "sqlite"; url = "file:./dev.db" }

model Product {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  name        String
  description String
  priceCents  Int
  imageUrl    String
  category    String
  stock       Int      @default(0)
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  orderItems  OrderItem[]
}

model Order {
  id           String      @id @default(cuid())
  customerName String
  email        String
  total        Int
  status       String      @default("pending")
  items        OrderItem[]
  createdAt    DateTime    @default(now())
}

model OrderItem {
  id        String  @id @default(cuid())
  orderId   String
  order     Order   @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  productId String
  product   Product @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id])

}

}

blocks.text: Cara Belajar Optimal Saat Mengerjakan

items: **Mulai dari skeleton dulu** — semua route ada, isinya kosong.
**Iterasi kecil** — selesaikan satu fitur (vertical slice), commit, lanjut.
**Pakai TypeScript strict mode** — kalau error, JANGAN `any`.
**Refactor saat ada duplikasi** — extract ke component / hook / util.
**Stuck > 30 menit** — istirahat, baca docs ulang, atau tanya tools (Anda boleh tanya saya juga).
**Setelah selesai, baca kode Anda dengan mata dingin** — biasanya banyak yang bisa diperbaiki.

blocks.text: Kriteria “Sudah Mahir”
Anda dianggap mahir kalau:

items: ✓ Bisa setup proyek Vite/Next.js + TS dari scratch tanpa lihat tutorial.
✓ Bisa membaca error TypeScript dan mengerti penyebabnya.
✓ Tahu kapan pakai `useState`, `useReducer`, Context, Zustand, Redux, atau TanStack Query.
✓ Bisa menulis custom hook generic yang reusable.
✓ Bisa men-debug performance dengan React DevTools Profiler.
✓ Bisa menulis test integration untuk komponen.
✓ Bisa memilih Server vs Client Component dengan benar di Next.js.
✓ Bisa menulis Server Action lengkap dengan validation & error handling.
✓ Tidak takut refactor kode lama — sudah punya safety net (TS + tests).
✓ Bisa membaca dokumentasi React/Next.js dan langsung paham.

blocks.text: Setelah Modul Ini

items: **Animation**: Framer Motion / React Spring.
**3D/Canvas**: Three.js + React Three Fiber.
**Maps**: Mapbox GL / Leaflet.
**Real-time**: Socket.io, Pusher, atau WebSocket native.
**Mobile**: React Native + Expo.
**Desktop**: Tauri + React.
**Micro-frontend**: Module Federation.
**Design system**: Storybook.
**Internationalization**: next-intl, react-i18next.
**Web Performance**: Core Web Vitals, Lighthouse audits.
**Accessibility**: WAI-ARIA, screen reader testing.

blocks.text: Selamat! Anda sudah punya peta jalan lengkap. Sisanya tinggal **konsistensi praktik**. Kerjakan proyek-proyek di atas, dan dalam 2-3 bulan Anda akan jauh lebih mahir dari sebelumnya.
Kalau ada yang ingin Anda dalami lebih lanjut atau butuh saya jelaskan ulang topik tertentu, tinggal beri tahu saya.

modules.summary: Selamat datang! Di tutorial ini kamu akan membangun satu aplikasi React utuh dari nol: Aplikasi Pencatat Keuangan.

blocks.text: Apa yang Akan Kita Bangun

Selamat datang! Di tutorial ini kamu akan membangun satu aplikasi React utuh dari nol: Aplikasi Pencatat Keuangan. Aplikasi ini mencatat pemasukan dan pengeluaran, menampilkan saldo, dan menyimpan datanya di browser sehingga tidak hilang saat halaman ditutup.
Fitur akhir aplikasi

items: Menambah transaksi (pemasukan / pengeluaran) lewat form.
Menampilkan daftar transaksi yang rapi.
Menghitung otomatis: total pemasukan, total pengeluaran, dan saldo.
Menghapus transaksi.
Memfilter transaksi (semua / pemasukan / pengeluaran).
Menyimpan data secara permanen di localStorage.
Tampilan rapi dan responsif, lalu di-deploy ke internet.

blocks.text: Yang perlu disiapkan

head: Kebutuhan
Keterangan
rows: Unduh dari nodejs.org, cek dengan: node -v
Sudah paham komponen, props, state, useState/useEffect

blocks.text: Ketik sendiri setiap potongan kode (jangan copy-paste semua). Mengetik membantu otot ingatanmu. Jalankan aplikasi setiap selesai satu bab agar tahu progresnya.

Saldo, total pemasukan, dan total pengeluaran tidak perlu disimpan di state tersendiri — semuanya bisa DIHITUNG dari daftar transaksi. Nilai yang dihitung dari state lain disebut derived state.

blocks.text: Tantangan Pengembangan Lanjutan
Aplikasi sudah jadi, tapi belajar terbaik adalah dengan mengembangkannya sendiri. Coba kerjakan tantangan berikut secara bertahap, dari mudah ke sulit.

Kamu sekarang punya pola lengkap membangun aplikasi React: state sebagai sumber kebenaran, komponen kecil yang fokus, data mengalir lewat props, dan logika yang dipakai ulang lewat custom hook. Ulangi pola ini di proyek-proyek berikutnya, dan kemampuanmu akan terus naik. Selamat berkarya!
blocks.title: Pesan penutup

modules.title: Pencatat Keuangan v2: useReducer & useContext
modules.summary: Di proyek v1, aplikasi Pencatat Keuangan baru memakai tiga hal: useState, useEffect, dan custom hook useLocalStorage.
modules.source: Proyek React Pencatat Keuangan v2 (Semua Hooks)

blocks.text: Tujuan & Peta Hook

Di proyek v1, aplikasi Pencatat Keuangan baru memakai tiga hal: useState, useEffect, dan custom hook useLocalStorage. Di v2 ini kita akan merombak dan memperluas aplikasi yang SAMA sehingga setiap React hook benar-benar terpakai pada fitur nyata. Tujuannya bukan sekadar 'menempel' hook, tetapi memahami kapan tiap hook memang menyelesaikan masalah.
Berikut peta rencana: hook mana dipakai untuk fitur apa. Kita kerjakan bertahap dari bab ke bab.

head: Hook
Fitur di aplikasi
rows: Input form & filter (sudah ada dari v1)
Simpan ke localStorage (sudah ada dari v1)
Berbagi state keuangan & tema gelap ke semua komponen
Handler stabil + item daftar tidak rerender percuma

blocks.text: Kerjakan berurutan; tiap bab membangun di atas bab sebelumnya. Di akhir tiap bab ada kotak Checkpoint dan rincian hook yang sudah direalisasikan.
blocks.title: Cara mengikuti

blocks.text: useReducer untuk Transaksi
Transaksi punya banyak aksi: tambah, hapus, edit, dan reset. Ini kandidat sempurna untuk useReducer agar semua logika perubahan terkumpul di satu tempat dan mudah diuji.

blocks.title: src/state/transaksiReducer.js

blocks.text: Di App, ganti useState transaksi dengan useReducer:

blocks.title: src/App.jsx (perubahan)

blocks.text:
State dengan banyak transisi yang saling terkait — reducer membuatnya rapi & terprediksi.
Reducer adalah fungsi murni sehingga gampang diuji terpisah dari komponen.
blocks.title: Kegunaan & kapan dipakai

blocks.text: useReducer — mengelola seluruh daftar transaksi lewat aksi (tambah/hapus/edit/reset/set).
blocks.title: Hook yang direalisasikan di bab ini

blocks.text: Aplikasi tetap berjalan seperti v1, tetapi state transaksi kini dikelola reducer, bukan useState.
blocks.title: Checkpoint

blocks.text: useContext: State Global & Tema
Agar komponen tidak perlu dioper props berlapis (dispatch, transaksi), kita bagikan lewat Context. Sekalian kita buat Context tema untuk fitur mode gelap.
Context Keuangan

blocks.title: src/state/KeuanganContext.jsx

blocks.text: Context Tema (Mode Gelap)

blocks.title: src/state/TemaContext.jsx

blocks.text: Bungkus aplikasi dengan kedua provider, lalu komponen mana pun bisa memanggil useKeuangan() atau useTema() tanpa prop drilling.

blocks.code:
// main.jsx
<TemaProvider>
  <KeuanganProvider>
    <App />
  </KeuanganProvider>
</TemaProvider>
blocks.title: src/main.jsx

blocks.text:
Berbagi data global ringan (state keuangan, tema, auth) ke banyak komponen di berbagai kedalaman.
Hindari untuk data yang sangat sering berubah & konsumen sangat banyak — semua konsumen ikut rerender.
blocks.title: Kegunaan & kapan dipakai

blocks.text:
useContext — mengakses state keuangan & tema dari komponen mana pun.
useReducer & useEffect — kini hidup di dalam Provider.
blocks.title: Hook yang direalisasikan di bab ini

blocks.text: Tombol mode gelap berfungsi, dan komponen membaca transaksi via useKeuangan() tanpa props.
blocks.title: Checkpoint

modules.title: Pencatat Keuangan v2: useMemo sampai useId
modules.summary: Ringkasan (pemasukan, pengeluaran, saldo) dan daftar terfilter dihitung dari transaksi.
modules.source: Proyek React Pencatat Keuangan v2 (Semua Hooks)

blocks.text: useMemo untuk Ringkasan & Filter
Ringkasan (pemasukan, pengeluaran, saldo) dan daftar terfilter dihitung dari transaksi. Saat transaksi banyak, komputasi ini sebaiknya di-cache dengan useMemo agar tidak diulang setiap render.

blocks.title: src/components/Ringkasan.jsx

blocks.text:
Komputasi turunan (filter/sum/sort) dari data yang bisa besar.
Menjaga referensi objek/array tetap stabil agar anak/efek tidak terpicu percuma.
blocks.title: Kegunaan & kapan dipakai

blocks.text: useMemo — menghitung ringkasan saldo sekali per perubahan transaksi.
blocks.title: Hook yang direalisasikan di bab ini

blocks.text: useCallback + React.memo
Daftar transaksi bisa panjang. Agar tiap baris tidak rerender saat ada perubahan yang tak berhubungan, kita bungkus item dengan React.memo dan jaga fungsi handler tetap stabil dengan useCallback.

blocks.title: src/components/ItemTransaksi.jsx

blocks.text:
useCallback: fungsi dioper ke anak ber-memo, atau jadi dependency efek.
React.memo: komponen yang sering dirender induk padahal props-nya jarang berubah.
blocks.title: Kegunaan & kapan dipakai

blocks.text: Dengan React Compiler aktif, useCallback & memo sering tidak perlu ditulis manual. Di sini kita tetap pelajari agar paham konsepnya.
blocks.title: Catatan 2026

blocks.text:
useCallback — menstabilkan handler hapus.
(plus React.memo pada ItemTransaksi).
blocks.title: Hook yang direalisasikan di bab ini

blocks.text: useRef: Auto-Fokus Input
Pengalaman pengguna lebih baik bila kursor langsung berada di input deskripsi saat halaman dibuka dan setelah menambah transaksi. useRef memberi akses langsung ke elemen DOM.

blocks.title: src/components/FormTransaksi.jsx

blocks.text:
Mengakses DOM: fokus, scroll, mengukur elemen, integrasi library non-React.
Menyimpan nilai mutable yang tidak perlu memicu render (mis. ID timer).
blocks.title: Kegunaan & kapan dipakai

blocks.text: useRef — referensi ke input deskripsi untuk auto-fokus.
blocks.title: Hook yang direalisasikan di bab ini

blocks.text: useImperativeHandle + forwardRef
Misalkan kita ingin tombol 'Transaksi Baru' di header yang, saat diklik, mem-fokus form dan mengosongkannya. Induk perlu memanggil method pada anak (form). Inilah kegunaan useImperativeHandle.

blocks.title: src/components/FormTransaksi.jsx

blocks.text:
Induk perlu memicu aksi imperatif pada anak: focus(), reset(), play(), scrollToTop().
Pakai hemat — utamakan props/state deklaratif; ini escape hatch untuk kasus imperatif.
blocks.title: Kegunaan & kapan dipakai

blocks.text: useImperativeHandle + forwardRef — mengekspos fokus()/reset() form ke induk.
blocks.title: Hook yang direalisasikan di bab ini

blocks.text: useId: Aksesibilitas Form
Agar label benar-benar terhubung ke input-nya (penting untuk pembaca layar dan klik label), tiap input butuh id unik. useId menjamin id unik & stabil meski form dipakai berkali-kali.

blocks.title: src/components/FieldDeskripsi.jsx

blocks.text:
Menghubungkan <label htmlFor> dengan <input id> tanpa bentrok saat komponen dipakai banyak kali.
JANGAN pakai useId untuk key list — key harus berasal dari data (t.id).
blocks.title: Kegunaan & kapan dipakai

blocks.text: useId — membuat id unik untuk pasangan label/input.
blocks.title: Hook yang direalisasikan di bab ini

modules.title: Pencatat Keuangan v2: Transition, LayoutEffect & External Store
modules.summary: Kita tambah kotak pencarian deskripsi. Bila transaksi sangat banyak, memfilter setiap ketikan bisa membuat input tersendat.
modules.source: Proyek React Pencatat Keuangan v2 (Semua Hooks)

blocks.text: Pencarian Mulus (useTransition + useDeferredValue)

Kita tambah kotak pencarian deskripsi. Bila transaksi sangat banyak, memfilter setiap ketikan bisa membuat input tersendat. useTransition menjaga input tetap responsif; useDeferredValue menunda render daftar berat.

blocks.title: src/components/PencarianTransaksi.jsx

blocks.text:
useTransition: update berat yang membuat UI tersendat (ganti filter/tab, daftar besar).
useDeferredValue: menunda render berat yang bergantung pada sebuah nilai (kata kunci pencarian).
blocks.title: Kegunaan & kapan dipakai

blocks.text:
useTransition — menandai ganti filter sebagai non-urgent.
useDeferredValue — menunda kata kunci untuk filtering.
useMemo — menghitung hasil filter.
blocks.title: Hook yang direalisasikan di bab ini

blocks.text: Mengetik di kotak cari tetap lancar walau daftar panjang; indikator 'Memperbarui...' muncul singkat saat ganti filter.
blocks.title: Checkpoint

blocks.text: useLayoutEffect: Bar Saldo Tanpa Kedip

Kita tambah bar visual proporsi pengeluaran terhadap pemasukan. Lebar bar dihitung dari ukuran kontainer lalu langsung diterapkan sebelum browser melukis, agar tidak ada kedipan dari 0 ke nilai akhir.

blocks.title: src/components/BarRasio.jsx

blocks.text: Default tetap useEffect. Pilih useLayoutEffect hanya saat kamu MENGUKUR DOM lalu langsung mengubah tampilannya dan ingin mencegah kedipan.
blocks.title: Pakai seperlunya

blocks.text: useLayoutEffect — mengukur lebar kontainer & set lebar bar sebelum paint.
blocks.title: Hook yang direalisasikan di bab ini

blocks.text: useDebugValue di Custom Hook
Kita rapikan logika simpan-muat ke custom hook useLocalStorage (seperti v1), dan tambahkan useDebugValue agar mudah dilihat di React DevTools.

blocks.title: src/hooks/useLocalStorage.js

blocks.text:
Memberi label informatif pada custom hook saat diinspeksi di DevTools.
Hanya berguna untuk custom hook; tak perlu untuk komponen biasa.
blocks.title: Kegunaan & kapan dipakai

blocks.text: useDebugValue — menampilkan ringkasan isi storage di DevTools.
blocks.title: Hook yang direalisasikan di bab ini

blocks.text: useSyncExternalStore: Sinkron Antar-Tab & Status Online

Karena data disimpan di localStorage, membuka aplikasi di dua tab bisa membuat data tidak sinkron. Kita berlangganan event 'storage' lewat useSyncExternalStore agar perubahan di tab lain langsung tampil. Sekalian, kita pantau status online.

modules.title: React Notes: Getting Started with React

blocks.text: Section 1.1: What is ReactJS?
ReactJS is an open-source, component based front end library responsible only for the **view layer** of the application. It is maintained by Facebook.

ReactJS uses virtual DOM based mechanism to fill in data (views) in HTML DOM. The virtual DOM works fast owning to the fact that it only changes individual DOM elements instead of reloading complete DOM every time

A React application is made up of multiple **components,** each responsible for outputting a small, reusable piece of HTML. Components can be nested within other components to allow complex applications to be built out of simple building blocks. A component may also maintain internal state - for example, a TabList component may store a variable corresponding to the currently open tab.

React allows us to write components using a domain-specific language called JSX. JSX allows us to write our components using HTML, whilst mixing in JavaScript events. React will internally convert this into a virtual DOM, and will ultimately output our HTML for us.

React *"reacts"* to state changes in your components quickly and automatically to rerender the components in the HTML DOM by utilizing the virtual DOM. The virtual DOM is an in-memory representation of an actual DOM. By doing most of the processing inside the virtual DOM rather than directly in the browser's DOM, React can act quickly and only add, update, and remove components which have changed since the last render cycle occurred.
Section 1.2: Installation or Setup

ReactJS is a JavaScript library contained in a single file `react-<version>.js` that can be included in any HTML page. People also commonly install the React DOM library `react-dom-<version>.js` along with the main React file:
**Basic Inclusion**

blocks.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head></head>
    <body>
    <script type="text/javascript" src="/path/to/react.js"></script>
    <script type="text/javascript" src="/path/to/react-dom.js"></script>
    <script type="text/javascript">
        // Use react JavaScript code here or in a separate file
    </script>
    </body>
</html>

blocks.text: To get the JavaScript files, go to the installation page of the official React documentation.

React also supports JSX syntax. JSX is an extension created by Facebook that adds XML syntax to JavaScript. In order to use JSX you need to include the Babel library and change `<script type="text/javascript">` to `<script type="text/babel">` in order to translate JSX to Javascript code.

blocks.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head></head>
    <body>
    <script type="text/javascript" src="/path/to/react.js"></script>
    <script type="text/javascript" src="/path/to/react-dom.js"></script>
    <script src="https://npmcdn.com/babel-core@5.8.38/browser.min.js"></script>
    <script type="text/babel">
        // Use react JSX code here or in a separate file
    </script>
    </body>
</html>

blocks.text: **Installing via npm**
You can also install React using npm by doing the following:
npm **install** --save react react-dom
To use React in your JavaScript project, you can do the following:
**Installing via Yarn**
Facebook released its own package manager named Yarn, which can also be used to install React. After installing Yarn you just need to run this command:
yarn add react react-dom
You can then use React in your project in exactly the same way as if you had installed React via npm.
Section 1.3: Hello World with Stateless Functions
Stateless components are getting their philosophy from functional programming. Which implies that: A function returns all time the same thing exactly on what is given to it.
**For example:**

As you can see from the above example that, statelessSum is always will return the same values given a and b. However, statefulSum function will not return the same values given even no parameters. This type of function's behaviour is also called as a *side-effect.* Since, the component affects somethings beyond.

So, it is advised to use stateless components more often, since they are *side-effect free* and will create the same behaviour always. That is what you want to be after in your apps because fluctuating state is the worst case scenario for a maintainable program.

The most basic type of react component is one without state. React components that are pure functions of their props and do not require any internal state management can be written as simple JavaScript functions. These are said to be `Stateless Functional Components` because they are a function only of `props,` without having any `state` to keep track of.
Here is a simple example to illustrate the concept of a `Stateless Functional Component:`
Note that all that this component does is render an `h1` element containing the `name` prop. This component doesn't keep track of any state. Here's an ES6 example as well:

Since these components do not require a backing instance to manage the state, React has more room for optimizations. The implementation is clean, but as of yet no such optimizations for stateless components have been implemented.
Section 1.4: Absolute Basics of Creating Reusable Components
**Components and Props**

As React concerns itself only with an application's view, the bulk of development in React will be the creation of components. A component represents a portion of the view of your application. "Props" are simply the attributes used on a JSX node (e.g. `<SomeComponent someProp="some prop's value"` />), and are the primary way our application interacts with our components. In the snippet above, inside of SomeComponent, we would have access to `this.props,` whose value would be the object `{someProp: "some prop's value"}.`

It can be useful to think of React components as simple functions - they take input in the form of "props", and produce output as markup. Many simple components take this a step further, making themselves "Pure Functions", meaning they do not issue side effects, and are idempotent (given a set of inputs, the component will always produce the same output). This goal can be formally enforced by actually creating components as functions, rather than "classes". There are three ways of creating a React component:
**Functional ("Stateless") Components**
**React.createClass()**
**ES2015 Classes**
These components are used in exactly the same way:
The above examples will all produce identical markup.
Functional components cannot have "state" within them. So if your component needs to have a state, then go for class based components. Refer Creating Components for more information.

As a final note, react props are immutable once they have been passed in, meaning they cannot be modified from within a component. If the parent of a component changes the value of a prop, React handles replacing the old props with the new, the component will rerender itself using the new values.
See Thinking In React and Reusable Components for deeper dives into the relationship of props to components.
Section 1.5: Create React App
create-react-app is a React app boilerplate generator created by Facebook. It provides a development environment configured for ease-of-use with minimal setup, including:
ES6 and JSX transpilation Dev server with hot module reloading Code linting CSS auto-prefixing Build script with JS, CSS and image bundling, and sourcemaps Jest testing framework
**Installation**
First, install create-react-app globally with node package manager (npm).

blocks.code: npm install -g create-react-app

blocks.text: Then run the generator in your chosen directory.

blocks.code: create-react-app my-app

blocks.text: Navigate to the newly created directory and run the start script.

blocks.code:
cd my-app/
npm start

blocks.text: **Configuration**
create-react-app is intentionally non-configurable by default. If non-default usage is required, for example, to use a compiled CSS language such as Sass, then the eject command can be used.

blocks.code: npm run eject

blocks.text: This allows editing of all configuration files. N.B. this is an irreversible process.
**Alternatives** Alternative React boilerplates include:
enclave nwb motion rackt-cli budō rwb quik sagui roc
**Build React App**
To build your app for production ready, run following command

blocks.code: npm run build

**Without JSX**
Here's a basic example that uses React's main API to create a React element and the React DOM API to render the React element in the browser.
**With JSX** Instead of creating a React element from strings one can use JSX (a Javascript extension created by Facebook for adding XML syntax to JavaScript), which allows to write

blocks.code: var rElement = React.createElement('h1', null, 'Hello, world!');

blocks.text: as the equivalent (and easier to read for someone familiar with HTML)

blocks.code:

Hello, world!

;

So finally the above example becomes:
Section 1.7: Hello World Component

A React component can be defined as an ES6 class that extends the base `React.Component` class. In its minimal form, a component *must* define a `render` method that specifies how the component renders to the DOM. The `render` method returns React nodes, which can be defined using JSX syntax as HTML-like tags. The following example shows how to define a minimal Component:

A Component can also receive `props.` These are properties passed by its parent in order to specify some values the component cannot know by itself; a property can also contain a function that can be called by the component after certain events occur - for example, a button could receive a function for its `onClick` property and call it whenever it is clicked. When writing a component, its `props` can be accessed through the `props` object on the Component itself:
The example above shows how the component can render an arbitrary string passed into the `name` prop by its parent. Note that a component cannot modify the props it receives.

A component can be rendered within any other component, or directly into the DOM if it's the topmost component, using `ReactDOM.render` and providing it with both the component and the DOM Node where you want the React tree to be rendered:

blocks.code:
import React from 'react'
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom'
import Hello from './Hello'

ReactDOM.render(<Hello name="Billy James" />, document.getElementById('main'))

For demo sake, let's make our Hello World app, display only the first name if a full name is given.
**Note:** Each component can have it's own state or accept it's parent's state as a prop.

blocks.text: Section 2.1: Creating Components
This is an extension of Basic Example:
**Basic Structure**
The above example is called a **stateless** component as it does not contain state (in the React sense of the word).
In such a case, some people find it preferable to use Stateless Functional Components, which are based on ES6 arrow functions.
**Stateless Functional Components**

In many applications there are smart components that hold state but render dumb components that simply receive props and return HTML as JSX. Stateless functional components are much more reusable and have a positive performance impact on your application.
They have 2 main characteristics:
1. When rendered they receive an object with all the props that were passed down 2. They must return the JSX to be rendered
**Stateful Components**

In contrast to the 'stateless' components shown above, 'stateful' components have a state object that can be updated with the `setState` method. The state must be initialized in the `constructor` before it can be set:

Extending a component with `PureComponent` instead of `Component` will automatically implement the `shouldComponentUpdate()` lifecycle method with shallow prop and state comparison. This keeps your application more performant by reducing the amount of un-necessary renders that occur. This assumes your components are 'Pure' and always render the same output with the same state and props input.
**Higher Order Components**
Higher order components (HOC) allow to share component functionality.
Higher order components are used when you want to share logic across several components regardless of how different they render.
Section 2.2: Basic Component
Given the following HTML file:
**index.html**
You can create a basic component using the following code in a separate file:
**scripts/example.js**
You will get the following result (note what is inside of `div#content):`

blocks.text: Section 2.3: Nesting Components
A lot of the power of ReactJS is its ability to allow nesting of components. Take the following two components:
You can nest and refer to those components in the definition of a different component:
Further nesting can be done in three ways, which all have their own places to be used.
**1. Nesting without using children**
This is the style where A composes B and B composes C.
**Pros**
Easy and fast to separate UI elements Easy to inject props down to children based on the parent component's state
**Cons**
Less visibility into the composition architecture Less reusability
**Good if**
B and C are just presentational components B should be responsible for C's lifecycle
**2. Nesting using children**
This is the style where A composes B and A tells B to compose C. More power to parent components.
**Pros**
Better components lifecycle management Better visibility into the composition architecture Better reusuability
**Cons** Injecting props can become a little expensive Less flexibility and power in child components
**Good if**
B should accept to compose something different than C in the future or somewhere else A should control the lifecycle of C

B would render C using `this.props.children,` and there isn't a structured way for B to know what those children are for. So, B may enrich the child components by giving additional props down, but if B needs to know exactly what they are, #3 might be a better option.
**3. Nesting using props**
This is the style where A composes B and B provides an option for A to pass something to compose for a specific purpose. More structured composition.
**Pros**
Composition as a feature Easy validation Better composaiblility
**Cons**
Injecting props can become a little expensive Less flexibility and power in child components
**Good if**
B has specific features defined to compose something B should only know how to render not what to render

#3 is usually a must for making a public library of components but also a good practice in general to make composable components and clearly define the composition features. #1 is the easiest and fastest to make something that works, but #2 and #3 should provide certain benefits in various use cases.
Section 2.4: Props
Props are a way to pass information into a React component, they can have any type including functions - sometimes referred to as callbacks.
In JSX props are passed with the attribute syntax

blocks.code: <MyComponent userID={123} />

blocks.text: Inside the definition for MyComponent userID will now be accessible from the props object
It's important to define all `props,` their types, and where applicable, their default value:

In this example the prop `someObject` is optional, but the prop `userID` is required. If you fail to provide `userID` to `MyComponent,` at runtime the React engine will show a console warning you that the required prop was not provided. Beware though, this warning is only shown in the development version of the React library, the production version will not log any warnings.
Using `defaultProps` allows you to simplify

blocks.code:
const { title = 'My Default Title' } = this.props;
console.log(title);

blocks.text: to

blocks.code: console.log(this.props.title);

blocks.text: It's also a safeguard for use of `object array` and `functions.` If you do not provide a default prop for an object, the following will throw an error if the prop is not passed:

blocks.code: if (this.props.someObject.someKey)

blocks.text: In example above, `this.props.someObject` is `undefined` and therefore the check of `someKey` will throw an error and the code will break. With the use of `defaultProps` you can safely use the above check.
Section 2.5: Component states - Dynamic user-interface

Suppose we want to have the following behaviour - We have a heading (say h3 element) and on clicking it, we want it to become an input box so that we can modify heading name. React makes this highly simple and intuitive using component states and if else statements. (Code explanation below)
The main part of the code is the **clickableTitle** variable. Based on the state variable **show,** it can be either be a Form element or a Button element. React allows nesting of components.
So we can add a {clickableTitle} element in the render function. It looks for the clickableTitle variable. Based on the value 'this.state.show', it displays the corresponding element.

Here you can find working example of it.
Section 2.7: setState pitfalls
You should use caution when using `setState` in an asynchronous context. For example, you might try to call `setState` in the callback of a get request:

This could call problems - if the callback is called after the `Component` is dismounted, then `this.setState` won't be a function. Whenever this is the case, you should be careful to ensure your usage of `setState` is cancellable.
In this example, you might wish to cancel the XHR request when the component dismounts:
The async method is saved as a state. In the `componentWillUnmount` you perform all your cleanup - including canceling the XHR request.

You could also do something more complex. In this example, I'm creating a 'stateSetter' function that accepts the this object as an argument and prevents `this.setState` when the function `cancel` has been called:
This works because the `cancelled` variable is visible in the `setState` closure we created.

modules.title: React Notes: JSX
modules.summary: There are several different ways to specify props in JSX.

blocks.text: Section 21.1: Props in JSX
There are several different ways to specify props in JSX.
**JavaScript Expressions**
You can pass **any JavaScript expression** as a prop, by surrounding it with `{}.` For example, in this JSX:

blocks.code: <MyComponent count={1 + 2 + 3 + 4} />

blocks.text: Inside the `MyComponent,` the value of `props.count` will be `10,` because the expression `1 + 2 + 3 + 4` gets evaluated.
If statements and for loops are not expressions in JavaScript, so they can't be used in JSX directly.
**String Literals**
Of course, you can just pass any `string literal` as a `prop` too. These two JSX expressions are equivalent:

blocks.code:
<MyComponent message="hello world" />
<MyComponent message={'hello world'} />

blocks.text: When you pass a string literal, its value is HTML-unescaped. So these two JSX expressions are equivalent:

blocks.code:
<MyComponent message="<3" />
<MyComponent message={'<3'} />

blocks.text: This behavior is usually not relevant. It's only mentioned here for completeness.
**Props Default Value**
If you pass no value for a prop, **it defaults to** `true.` These two JSX expressions are equivalent:

blocks.code:
<MyTextBox autocomplete />
<MyTextBox autocomplete={true} />

blocks.text: However, the React team says in their docs **using this approach is not recommended,** because it can be confused with the ES6 object shorthand `{foo}` which is short for `{foo: foo}` rather than `{foo: true}.` They say this behavior is just there so that it matches the behavior of HTML.
**Spread Attributes**
If you already have props as an object, and you want to pass it in JSX, you can use `...` as a spread operator to pass the whole props object. These two components are equivalent:
Section 21.2: Children in JSX
In JSX expressions that contain both an opening tag and a closing tag, the content between those tags is passed as a special prop: `props.children.` There are several different ways to pass children:
**String Literals**
You can put a string between the opening and closing tags and `props.children` will just be that string. This is useful for many of the built-in HTML elements. For example:

blocks.code: Hello world!

blocks.text:
This is valid JSX, and `props.children` in MyComponent will simply be `

Hello world!

.`
Note that **the HTML is unescaped,** so you can generally write JSX just like you would write HTML.
Bare in mind, that in this case JSX:

removes whitespace at the beginning and ending of a line; removes blank lines; new lines adjacent to tags are removed; new lines that occur in the middle of string literals are condensed into a single space.
**JSX Children**
You can provide more JSX elements as the children. This is useful for displaying nested components:

blocks.code:
<MyContainer>
  <MyFirstComponent />
  <MySecondComponent />
</MyContainer>

blocks.text: You can **mix together different types of children, so you can use string literals together with JSX children.** This is another way in which JSX is like HTML, so that this is both valid JSX and valid HTML:

blocks.code:
Here is a list

  • Item 1
  • Item 2

blocks.text: Note that a React component **can't return multiple React elements, but a single JSX expression can have multiple children.** So if you want a component to render multiple things you can wrap them in a `div` like the example above.
**JavaScript Expressions**
You can pass any JavaScript expression as children, by enclosing it within `{}.` For example, these expressions are equivalent:

blocks.code:
<MyComponent>foo</MyComponent>
<MyComponent>{'foo'}</MyComponent>

blocks.text: This is often useful for rendering a list of JSX expressions of arbitrary length. For example, this renders an HTML list:
Note that JavaScript expressions can be mixed with other types of children.
**Functions as Children**

Normally, JavaScript expressions inserted in JSX will evaluate to a string, a React element, or a list of those things. However, `props.children` works just like any other prop in that it can pass any sort of data, not just the sorts that React knows how to render. For example, if you have a custom component, you could have it take a callback as props.children:

Children passed to a custom component can be anything, as long as that component transforms them into something React can understand before rendering. This usage is not common, but it works if you want to stretch what JSX is capable of.
**Ignored Values**
Note that `false, null, undefined,` and `true` are valid children. But they simply don't render. These JSX expressions will all render to the same thing:

blocks.code:
<MyComponent />
<MyComponent></MyComponent>
<MyComponent>{false}</MyComponent>
<MyComponent>{null}</MyComponent>
<MyComponent>{true}</MyComponent>

blocks.text: This is extremely useful to conditionally render React elements. This JSX only renders a if `showHeader` is true:

blocks.code:
{showHeader &&
}

blocks.text: One important caveat is that some "falsy" values, such as the `0` number, are still rendered by React. For example, this code will not behave as you might expect because `0` will be printed when `props.messages` is an empty array:

blocks.code: {props.messages.length && }

blocks.text: One approach to fix this is to make sure that the expression before the `&&` is always boolean:

blocks.code: {props.messages.length > 0 && }

blocks.text: Lastly, bare in mind that if you want a value like `false, true, null,` or `undefined` to appear in the output, you have to convert it to a string first:

blocks.code: My JavaScript variable is {String(myVariable)}.

modules.title: React Notes: State in React
modules.summary: State in React components is essential to manage and communicate data in your application.

blocks.text: Section 4.1: Basic State

State in React components is essential to manage and communicate data in your application. It is represented as a JavaScript object and has *component level* scope, it can be thought of as the private data of your component.
In the example below we are defining some initial state in the `constructor` function of our component and make use of it in the `render` function.
Section 4.2: Common Antipattern
You should not save `props` into `state.` It is considered an anti-pattern. For example:
The prop `url` is saved on `state` and then modified. Instead, choose to save the changes to a state, and then build the full path using both `state` and `props:`

This is because in a React application we want to have a single source of truth - i.e. all data is the responsibility of one single component, and only one component. It is the responsibility of this component to store the data within its state, and distribute the data to other components via props.

In the first example, both the MyComponent class and its parent are maintaining 'url' within their state. If we update state.url in MyComponent, these changes are not reflected in the parent. We have lost our single source of truth, and it becomes increasingly difficult to track the flow of data through our application. Contrast this with the second example - url is only maintained in the state of the parent component, and utilised as a prop in MyComponent - we therefore maintain a single source of truth.
Section 4.3: setState()

The primary way that you make UI updates to your React applications is through a call to the `setState()` function. This function will perform a *shallow merge* between the new state that you provide and the previous state, and will trigger a re-render of your component and all decedents.
**Parameters**
1. `updater:` It can be an object with a number of key-value pairs that should be merged into the state or a function that returns such an object.

2. `callback (optional):` a function which will be executed after `setState()` has been executed successfully. Due to the fact that calls to `setState()` are not guaranteed by React to be atomic, this can sometimes be useful if you want to perform some action after you are positive that `setState()` has been executed successfully.
**Usage:**

The `setState` method accepts an `updater` argument that can either be an object with a number of key-value-pairs that should be merged into the state, or a function that returns such an object computed from `prevState` and props.
**Using** `setState()` **with an Object as** `updater`
**Using** `setState()` **with a Function as** `updater`

This can be safer than using an object argument where multiple calls to `setState()` are used, as multiple calls may be batched together by React and executed at once, and is the preferred approach when using current props to set state.
These calls may be batched together by React using `Object.assign(),` resulting in the counter being incremented by 1 rather than 3.
The functional approach can also be used to move state setting logic outside of components. This allows for isolation and re-use of state logic.
**Calling** `setState()` **with an Object and a callback function**

modules.title: React Notes: Props in React
modules.summary: props are used to pass data and methods from a parent component to a child component.

blocks.text: Section 5.1: Introduction
`props` are used to pass data and methods from a parent component to a child component.
**Interesting things about** `props`
1. They are immutable.
2. They allow us to create reusable components.
**Basic example**
As you can see in the example, thanks to `props` we can create reusable components.
Section 5.2: Default props

`defaultProps` allows you to set default, or fallback, values for your component `props. defaultProps` are useful when you call components from different views with fixed props, but in some views you need to pass different value.
**Syntax**
The result of `getDefaultProps()` or `defaultProps` will be cached and used to ensure that `this.props.randomObject` will have a value if it was not specified by the parent component.
Section 5.3: PropTypes

`propTypes` allows you to specify what `props` your component needs and the type they should be. Your component will work without setting `propTypes,` but it is good practice to define these as it will make your component more readable, act as documentation to other developers who are reading your component, and during development, React will warn you if you you try to set a prop which is a different type to the definition you have set for it.
Some primitive `propTypes` and commonly useable `propTypes` are -

Section 5.4: Passing down props using spread operator
Instead of

blocks.code: var component = <Component foo={this.props.x} bar={this.props.y} />;

blocks.text: Remember that the properties of the object that you pass in are copied onto the component's props.
The order is important. Later attributes override previous ones.
Another case is that you also can use spread operator to pass only parts of props to children components, then you can use destructuring syntax from props again.
It's very useful when children components need lots of props but not want pass them one by one.
Section 5.5: Props.children and component composition

The "child" components of a component are available on a special prop, `props.children.` This prop is very useful for "Compositing" components together, and can make JSX markup more intuitive or reflective of the intended final structure of the DOM:
